cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Front-end development is building what runs in the user's browser: HTML for structure and meaning, CSS for presentation, and JavaScript for interactivity and talking to APIs.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Core skills: how the browser loads and renders a page (DNS, TCP, TLS, HTTP), the DOM and semantic HTML, the cascade and box model, the event-driven model and async JavaScript, accessible and responsive UIs, components with clear state, where rendering happens, and shipping fast tested code through a build pipeline and CDN.

questions.q: If the app works in your browser, is the front end finished?
questions.a: No. Your laptop is fast. It may be slow on a mid-range phone on a mobile network or unusable with a keyboard or screen reader.
The tree of nodes the browser builds from HTML, which JavaScript reads and changes.

questions.q: Why use semantic HTML instead of divs?
questions.a: Elements like header, nav and article carry meaning that browsers, assistive tech and search engines can use.
